Suggest trial layouts from the number of entries and available field space

Source: R/design_options.R
design_options.Rd

Lists parameter options for the package's three design families, starting with the information the breeder knows. Rows, columns and check counts can be left unspecified. No randomization or optimization is performed.

Usage

design_options(
  n_entries,
  design = c("augmented_row_column", "prep", "resolvable"),
  n_checks = NULL,
  rows = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  n_locations = 1L,
  n_reps = 2:3,
  block_size = c(5L, 8L, 10L, 12L, 16L, 20L),
  prep_prop = NULL,
  max_plots = NULL,
  max_dimension = NULL,
  min_error_df = 1L,
  n_options = 6L,
  n_candidates = 200L
)

Arguments

n_entries

Number of test entries, excluding checks.

design

Design families to consider: "augmented_row_column" (augmented row-column), "prep" (partially replicated), and "resolvable" (fully replicated row-column). Defaults to all three.

n_checks

Distinct check genotypes to consider, a non-negative integer or vector. NULL tries 2 through 6 for augmented row-column designs and zero for the other families. p-rep uses no separate checks; it is excluded when only positive check counts are requested. Resolvable designs replicate checks just like the other genotypes.

rows, cols

Known field dimensions, per location, including all replicates. Each can be a positive integer, a vector of dimensions to consider, or NULL to search automatically. Supplied dimensions are exact candidate sizes, not upper bounds. For p-rep, the last row may be partially occupied, but wholly empty final rows are not proposed.

n_locations

Number of locations. Augmented row-column and resolvable layouts describe one field to randomize independently at each location. A p-rep option describes the combined multi-location design.

n_reps

Full replication counts to try for resolvable designs (at least 2). Other design families use their own replication scheme.

block_size

Maximum incomplete block sizes to try for p-rep.

prep_prop

Proportions of entries to duplicate at each p-rep location. Counts use round(n_entries * prep_prop), as in the generator. An entry may be duplicated at only one location, so the sum of these counts over locations must not exceed n_entries. NULL tries 15%, 20% and 25%, and, for several locations, a balanced share of entries per location rounded down to respect this budget.

max_plots

Largest field area (rows times columns) per location. Defaults to four times the number of genotypes (increased when more full replicates are requested), or the largest supplied field area when both dimensions are given.

max_dimension

Largest automatically searched row or column dimension. Defaults to twice the square root of max_plots, with a minimum of 20. Explicit dimensions are not restricted by this bound. When neither dimension is supplied, fields with an aspect ratio above 3 are excluded. Supply a dimension explicitly to consider longer fields.

min_error_df

Minimum nominal error degrees of freedom. These are count-based values for the design model, assuming its effects are estimable, not degrees of freedom of a later spatial model.

n_options

Maximum options returned per design family. The shortlist includes different check, full-replication or p-rep counts before adding further layouts with the same counts.

n_candidates

Search candidates to pass to the augmented row-column and p-rep generators. Defaults to 200. This is a user-selected search effort, not a dimension inferred from entry counts.

Value

A tibble with option id, design family, entry/check counts, field dimensions, location and replication counts, active plots per location and in total, field area, unused positions, check plots, repeated entries, blocks, nominal error_df, method and notes. Field dimensions are named rows_in_field and cols_in_field, matching augmented_row_column_design(). Block and replicate dimensions are included where applicable. n_candidates reports the chosen search effort. checks_per_block is a list-column with each augmented row-column option's check-allocation matrix, or NULL for the default complete check blocks. These columns support an explicit generator call. generator names the function to call; arguments is a list-column of its layout arguments. Add your own treatments, controls (augmented row-column) and seed before calling it with do.call(). p-rep arguments include placeholder location names, which can be replaced with your own names. Attribute diagnostics reports the number of shortlisted options and the reason for any excluded family. No matches return a typed empty tibble and a message suggesting which constraints to relax.

Details

This is a parameter planner. Candidates pass plot-count, block-size and nominal error-df checks. Augmented row-column candidates also pass the check coverage and row/column group conditions used by the generator. p-rep candidates have enough repeated plots to connect their blocks and a pair-count budget compatible with (0,1) concurrence. These necessary conditions do not certify a randomized design's connectivity or efficiency: generate the chosen option, inspect its summary and run check_design(). The search is bounded and not exhaustive.

Augmented row-column options use equal row and column groups. Every block has at least n_checks rows and at least n_checks columns, leaving room for one copy of each check in a distinct row and column. For example, four checks require blocks of at least 4 rows by 4 columns. Every block contains all checks at least once; extra positions are assigned to extra check replication, so the number of test-entry positions is exactly n_entries. Flexible allocations use method = "optimal".

Resolvable options may contain filler positions, which are reported in unused_plots. Include both entries and checks in the generator's treatments. Its native generator treats them all as treatments; if checks need to be marked in Breedbase, set is_control in both the generated design and breedbase_design tables before saving.

Within each resource-count group, smaller field areas, fewer unused positions and less elongated fields come first; Latin augmented row-column constructions are preferred over searched allocations at the same area. This ordering does not estimate statistical precision or choose the biologically best design.

See also

augmented_row_column_layouts(), augmented_prep_parameters(), augmented_row_column_design(), augmented_prep_design(), resolvable_row_column_design()

Examples

# Only the number of entries is known:
options <- design_options(100)
options[, c("option", "design", "n_checks", "rows_in_field", "cols_in_field", "plots_per_location")]
#> # A tibble: 18 × 6
#>    option design         n_checks rows_in_field cols_in_field plots_per_location
#>     <int> <chr>             <int>         <int>         <int>              <dbl>
#>  1      1 augmented_row…        2             9            14                126
#>  2      2 augmented_row…        3             9            14                126
#>  3      3 augmented_row…        4             9            14                126
#>  4      4 augmented_row…        5             8            16                128
#>  5      5 augmented_row…        6            10            13                130
#>  6      6 augmented_row…        2             9            14                126
#>  7      7 prep                  0            13             9                115
#>  8      8 prep                  0            10            12                120
#>  9      9 prep                  0             9            14                125
#> 10     10 prep                  0            13             9                115
#> 11     11 prep                  0            12            10                120
#> 12     12 prep                  0             9            14                125
#> 13     13 resolvable            0            20            10                200
#> 14     14 resolvable            0            20            15                300
#> 15     15 resolvable            0            10            20                200
#> 16     16 resolvable            0            15            20                300
#> 17     17 resolvable            0            10            20                200
#> 18     18 resolvable            0            12            25                300

# A known field, four checks and exactly 108 test entries:
options <- design_options(108, design = "augmented_row_column", n_checks = 4,
                          rows = 12, cols = 12, n_candidates = 5)
selected <- options[1, ]
trial <- augmented_row_column_design(
  treatments = paste0("LINE_", seq_len(108)),
  controls = paste0("CHECK_", seq_len(selected$n_checks)),
  rows_in_field = selected$rows_in_field,
  cols_in_field = selected$cols_in_field,
  rows_per_block = selected$rows_per_block,
  cols_per_block = selected$cols_per_block,
  checks_per_block = selected$checks_per_block[[1]],
  method = selected$method,
  n_candidates = selected$n_candidates,
  seed = 2026
)

# Fully replicated options with one known dimension:
design_options(42, design = "resolvable", cols = 7, n_reps = 3)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 27
#>   option design     n_entries n_checks rows_in_field cols_in_field n_locations
#>    <int> <chr>          <int>    <int>         <int>         <int>       <int>
#> 1      1 resolvable        42        0            18             7           1
#> 2      2 resolvable        42        0            21             7           1
#> 3      3 resolvable        42        0            24             7           1
#> 4      4 resolvable        42        0            27             7           1
#> # ℹ 20 more variables: n_reps <int>, rows_per_block <int>,
#> #   cols_per_block <int>, rows_per_rep <dbl>, cols_per_rep <int>,
#> #   block_size <int>, n_candidates <int>, checks_per_block <list>,
#> #   plots_per_location <dbl>, total_plots <dbl>, field_plots <dbl>,
#> #   unused_plots <dbl>, check_plots <int>, n_repeated <dbl>, n_blocks <dbl>,
#> #   error_df <dbl>, method <chr>, generator <chr>, arguments <list>, note <chr>
# Partial replication at three locations:
design_options(100, design = "prep", n_locations = 3)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 27
#>   option design n_entries n_checks rows_in_field cols_in_field n_locations

#> 2      2 prep         100        0            10            12           3

#> 5      5 prep         100        0            13             9           3
